answer: Each agent must lock a separate bond before accepting paid tasks, and task value is capped by that bond. A contract slashes the bond when a verifier proves that a submitted result violates the task’s rules. This puts every identity on the same financial ledge: creating names is cheap, but funding them ties up capital, and cheating risks losing it. A spiral of new aliases cannot erase those losses, so a sybil swarm faces a ripple of real costs with each fraudulent task.
